'''Henry Ralph Mahler''' (1921–1983) was an [[Austria]]n-born American biochemist known for his research in the fields of [[neurochemistry|both mitochondrial biogenesis and neurochemistry]].

==Biography==
Mahler was born in 1921 in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]]. He emigrated to [[the United States]] in 1938, where he enrolled in [[Swarthmore College]], from which he graduating in 1943. The same year, he enrolled at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he received his Ph.D. in 1948. At Berkeley, he conducted research on aspects of mechanism of photosynthesis in plant [[chloroplast]]s under the direction of Nobel Prize winner [[Melvin Calvin]].<ref name=cotman>{{Cite journal |last=Cotman |first=Carl W. |date=April 1984 |title=In Memoriam: Henry R. Mahler 1921-1983 |journal=Journal of Neurochemistry |language=en |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=1200–1202 |doi=10.1111/j.1471-4159.1984.tb12733.x |pmid=6366121 |s2cid=2925790 |issn=0022-3042}}</ref> He then completed his [[postdoc]] at the [[Texas Research Foundation]] before joining the faculty of the [[University of Wisconsin, Madison]]'s Institute for Enzyme Research in 1949 as a senior research associate. In 1951, he became an assistant professor there.<ref name=memorial>{{Cite web |url=http://webapp1.dlib.indiana.edu/bfc/view?docId=B10-1984&chunk.id=d1e97&toc.id=&brand=bfc |title=Memorial Resolution Research Professor Henry R. Mahler |date=1983-11-01 |website=Indiana University Bloomington Faculty Council Circular  |access-date=2018-09-02}}</ref>

In 1955, he moved to [[Bloomington, Indiana|Bloomington]], [[Indiana]] to join the faculty of [[Indiana University]] as an associate professor. He was promoted to full professor at Indiana University in 1957, and was named research professor of biochemistry and neural sciences as well as National Institutes of Health Research Career Investigator there in 1966. In the 1976–77 academic year, he served as an honor fellow at [[University College London]], a visiting professor at the C.N.R.S. Institute of Molecular Genetics, [[Gif-sur-Yvette]], [[France]], and visiting professor at the Institut fur Allgemeine Biochemie of the [[University of Vienna]].<ref name=memorial/> During Professor Mahler's career, he published more than 300 research articles with his many former students, postdoctoral fellows and colleagues. He also coauthored two editions (1966 and 1971) of a well known textbook ''Biological Chemistry'' with his colleague Professor Eugene H. Cordes.  In 1972, he collaborated with his Indiana University colleague [[Rudolf Raff]] on a paper criticizing the theory that [[mitochondria]] in the cells of higher organisms originated as independent, [[single-celled organism]]s.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=1972-08-31 |title=Monitor |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tMUKmNZwPrsC |magazine=New Scientist |language=en |publisher=Reed Business Information |page=421 |access-date=2018-09-02}}</ref> 
He died on July 6, 1983, of [[heart failure]] at [[Woods Hole, Massachusetts|Woods Hole]], [[Massachusetts]].<ref name=cotman/>
